data.description:
## Discovered from

rebar-debug on bug `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` (3a52-2d79-320d-4fed), root cause RC-B. See
that ticket's "Phase 1 EXIT" comment for the full evidence trail.

## Problem

Two independent gaps leave the snapshot store with no size-based reclaim at all.

**1. The backstop does not exist.** `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md:72-73` and
the janitor module's own contract docstring (`src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:13-15`) both state
that reclamation is driven by a free-space watermark "backstopped by the incrementally-
maintained byte total". `_gc_pass` (`janitor.py:303-345`) reads only `free`
(`shutil.disk_usage`) and each entry's `mtime`. It never consults `_cache.byte_total`. The only
reader is `startup_sweep` (`janitor.py:251`), and that is reconciliation, not eviction. There
is no store-size cap knob in the config surface either (`docs/config.md:474-484`).

**2. The dominant consumer is not byte-accounted.** `cache.acquire` calls
`add_bytes(entry_size(dest))` at `src/rebar/_snapshot/cache.py:203`, but `materialize_tickets`
(`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:616-708`) bypasses `acquire` entirely and never calls
`add_bytes`. The `tickets-<sha>` entries are ~620 MiB each and are the largest thing in the
store, so even if the backstop above were implemented it would under-count them to **zero**.

(`_is_entry` at `janitor.py:110-122` does recognise `tickets-` entries as evictable, so GC
would remove them if a trigger ever fired — the gap is purely in the trigger and the
accounting.)

## Impact

On the review-bot host this contributed to `rebar-root-disk-pressure` breaching 85% and
reaching 90% with nothing reclaiming: the free-space trigger is unreachable below 93.3% used on
that volume (tracked on 3a52), the 7-day cold-trim exceeds the container's lifetime, and the
third trigger the ADR promises is absent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_gc_pass` gains a byte-total-driven eviction trigger with a documented, configurable cap
      (or ADR 0005 and the janitor docstring are corrected to remove the promise — but then the
      store has only one working trigger, so the cap is the expected resolution).
- [ ] `materialize_tickets` records its entries in the store's byte total, so the accounting
      reflects the entries that actually dominate it.
- [ ] A test observes the untracked bytes RED (a store whose real size far exceeds the reported
      `byte_total`) and GREEN after the fix.
- [ ] `docs/config.md`, `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` and `docs/env-vars.md` document the new
      cap knob (a docs test pins these — `tests/unit/test_snapshot_docs.py`).
data.title: Snapshot janitor's ADR-promised byte-total backstop is unimplemented, and materialize_tickets never byte-accounts its entries
